record.paper_title: Open Questions in Charm Decays Deserving an Answer
record.original_question: What is the neutral-charm mixing rate r_D = Gamma(D^0 -> l^- X)/Gamma(D^0 -> l^+ X), and can experiments push the sensitivity below 10^-4 or even down to about 10^-5 so that a nonzero D^0-anti-D^0 oscillation signal can be established and interpreted despite the Standard Model's long-distance uncertainties?

evidence.quote: According to the SM the rate for D0 − D¯ 0 oscillations is quite slow, namely rD ≡ Γ(D0 → l−X) / Γ(D0 → l+X) ∼ O(10−4 ).
Observing a non-vanishing value for rD between 10−4 and 10−3 would at present not constitute irrefutable evidence for NP, considering the uncertainties in the SM prediction.
Can D0 − D¯ 0 oscillations be probed down to rd ∼ 10−5 , which almost certainly should reveal a positive signal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the neutral charm meson system consisting of $D^0$ and $\bar D^0$, which mix via flavor oscillations. Define the time-integrated wrong-sign semileptonic rate ratio
$$r_D \;=\; \frac{\Gamma(D^0 \to \ell^- X)}{\Gamma(D^0 \to \ell^+ X)},$$
where the numerator counts semileptonic decays of an initially tagged $D^0$ to a "wrong-sign" lepton (only possible after oscillation into $\bar D^0$) and the denominator counts the corresponding right-sign decays. Within the Standard Model, short-distance contributions place $r_D$ well below $10^{-6}$, but long-distance hadronic contributions are estimated to push $r_D$ up to order $10^{-4}$, with sizeable theoretical uncertainty.

(a) Determine the value of $r_D$.

(b) Decide whether experimental measurements of $D^0$–$\bar D^0$ oscillations can be made sensitive at the level $r_D \lesssim 10^{-4}$, and further whether the sensitivity can be improved to roughly $r_D \sim 10^{-5}$, a level at which a nonzero oscillation signal is expected to be unambiguously detected and meaningfully interpreted despite the Standard Model long-distance uncertainties in the prediction.
artifact.status_search_result: $D^0$–$\bar D^0$ mixing has been observed and is now firmly established (combined evidence above 5σ since 2012, with LHCb and Belle measurements). Current experimental sensitivities for the mixing parameters $x$ and $y$ reach the $10^{-5}$ level, well below the originally targeted $r_D \lesssim 10^{-4}$, so the experimental aspect of the question is resolved. However, interpreting the observed mixing as evidence for or against New Physics remains hampered by long-distance Standard Model uncertainties, so the interpretive part is not fully settled.

status_evidence.title: PDG Review: D0–D0bar Mixing (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Review of established D0-D0bar mixing parameters at the 10^-3 to 10^-5 level.
status_evidence.claim: Mixing is established and parameters are measured at sensitivities reaching 10^-5.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of D0–D0bar mixing parameters and search for CP violation using D0→K+π- decays
status_evidence.snippet: LHCb measurement of mixing parameters with x'^2 at the 10^-5 level.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental sensitivity to mixing observables has reached the 10^-5 regime.

status_evidence.title: Updated determination of D0–D0bar mixing and CP violation parameters
status_evidence.snippet: R_D ≈ 3.45×10^-3 measured with high precision by LHCb.
status_evidence.claim: Wrong-sign rate parameters are measured with high precision, far surpassing 10^-4 sensitivity.
